displayedInputs.question: How many ways are there to place \(3\) indistinguishable red chips, \(3\) indistinguishable blue chips, and \(3\) indistinguishable green chips in the squares of a \(3 \times 3\) grid so that no two chips of the same color are directly adjacent to each other, either vertically or horizontally?
How many integer values of \(x\) satisfy \(|x| < 3\pi?\)

In an after-school program for juniors and seniors, there is a debate team with an equal number of students from each class on the team. Among the \(28\) students in the program, \(25\%\) of the juniors and \(10\%\) of the seniors are on the debate team. How many juniors are in the program?

At a math contest, \(57\) students are wearing blue shirts, and another \(75\) students are wearing yellow shirts. The \(132\) students are assigned into \(66\) pairs. In exactly \(23\) of these pairs, both students are wearing blue shirts. In how many pairs are both students wearing yellow shirts?

The ages of Jonie’s four cousins are distinct single-digit positive integers. Two of the cousins’ ages multiplied together give \(24,\) while the other two multiply to \(30.\) What is the sum of the ages of Jonie’s four cousins?

Ms. Blackwell gives an exam to two classes. The mean of the scores of the students in the morning class is \(84,\) and the afternoon class’s mean score is \(70.\) The ratio of the number of students in the morning class to the number of students in the afternoon class is \(\frac{3}{4}.\) What is the mean of the scores of all the students?

In a plane, four circles with radii \(1,\) \(3,\) \(5,\) and \(7\) are tangent to line \(\ell\) at the same point \(A,\) but they may be on either side of \(\ell.\) Region \(S\) consists of all the points that lie inside exactly one of the four circles. What is the maximum possible area of region \(S?\)

The point \(P(a,b)\) in the \(xy\)-plane is first rotated counterclockwise by \(90^\circ\) around the point \((1,5)\) and then reflected about the line \(y = -x.\) The image of \(P\) after these two transformations is at \((-6,3).\) What is \(b - a ?\)

An inverted cone with base radius \(12 \mathrm{ cm}\) and height \(18 \mathrm{ cm}\) is full of water. The water is poured into a tall cylinder whose horizontal base has a radius of \(24 \mathrm{ cm}.\) What is the height in centimeters of the water in the cylinder?

mappings.rationale: Tangency at A makes circles on the same side nested, while opposite-side interiors are disjoint. Optimize the exactly-one area either by enumerating side partitions and subtracting nested disk areas, or by bounding the contribution of the two largest disks and exhibiting equality.
mappings.answerReason: If radii 7 and 5 are on opposite sides, their disks have total area 74π. The radius-3 disk excludes at least 9π from the exactly-one region, so S≤65π. Equality occurs with {7} opposite {1,3,5}, giving 49π+(25−9)π=65π. If radii 7 and 5 share a side, S≤(49−25+9)π=33π.

mappings.rationale: Apply the coordinate effects of a right-angle rotation about a non-origin center and a reflection in an oblique line. Translating relative to the rotation center supports the rotation calculation.
mappings.answerReason: Rotation about (1,5) sends (a,b) to (6−b,a+4). Reflection in y=−x then gives (−a−4,b−6). Equating this to (−6,3) yields a=2 and b=9, so b−a=7.

mappings.rationale: Conserve the water volume between a full cone and a partially filled cylinder, using their respective volume formulas.
mappings.answerReason: The cone contains (1/3)π·12²·18=864π cubic centimeters. Therefore π·24²·h=864π, giving h=864/576=1.5 centimeters.
